posts.legenda: Two threads each increment the same counter a million times in C. Why does the total fall short of two million? The animation shows an illustrative lost update, a section protected by a mutex, and the indivisible increment performed by atomic_fetch_add. In C, the data race in the unprotected version has undefined behavior; the diagram is not an execution trace. Measured on this machine: gcc 15.2.0, -O2 -pthread, Ryzen 7 5700U, 15 runs per version on November 1, 2026. Median times: no protection, 11.0 ms with an incorrect total; mutex, 92.2 ms; atomic, 21.4 ms. Mutex and atomic reached 2,000,000 in all 15 runs. These results apply to this program and environment, not a general performance rule. Sources for the explanation: C11/WG14 N1570, sections 5.1.2.4 and 7.17.7.5: https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf pthread_mutex_lock documentation: https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19120-01/open.solaris/816-5137/sync-117/index.html Want to see how concurrency works in another language? Comment which one you want next. This is my voice, cloned with AI. Original animations created for this demonstration. #Shorts #CProgramming #Concurrency #Mutex #Atomic

evidencia.defesas: data futura, canal ativo, sem duplicata na fila

riscos: O Postiz não garante idempotência: se o envio falhar, consultar a fila antes de repetir.
A API não marca conteúdo alterado ou sintético: com voz ou imagem gerada, marcar à mão na rede.
Depois de publicar: conferir no Studio (ERROR no Postiz não prova falha), fixar o primeiro comentário e marcar o conteúdo alterado, tudo à mão.
como_desfazer: Antes do horário: apagar o post no Postiz (os ids saem no registro e em `vp postiz posts`). Depois do horário: apagar a publicação na rede; o Postiz não desfaz o que já saiu.
